title: OpenAI Preparedness Framework and DeepMind Frontier Safety Framework

questions.question: Two labs track the same model capability but assign it different policy categories. What should a policy reader compare?
options: The classification and what action that category triggers
The number of pages in each framework
The order in which each lab announced its framework
The model names used in the policy examples
questions.explanation: Compare the category with its consequence—whether it triggers reports and mitigation or monitoring only. Page count, announcement order, and model examples do not tell you what action the category requires.

questions.question: Under OpenAI Preparedness Framework v2 as described here, what is the key consequence of a Research Category?
options: It is monitored but does not automatically trigger mitigations
It automatically requires a public safeguards report
It is excluded from future capability evaluations
It requires an immediate training pause in every case
questions.explanation: Research Categories are monitored but do not automatically trigger mitigations; Tracked Categories trigger reports and review. An immediate pause would overstate the consequence assigned to a Research Category.

questions.question: How does DeepMind FSF v3 represent autonomy in the lesson's summary?
options: It is a separate top-level domain in every table
It is folded into ML R&D and Cyber domains
It is treated only as a user-content safety category
It is excluded from capability tracking
questions.explanation: DeepMind folds autonomy into ML R&D and Cyber rather than naming it as a standalone top-level domain. Calling it separate in every table reverses that structural choice.

questions.question: A model strategically underperforms during evaluations. Which risk term from the lesson names this behavior?
options: Sandbagging
Long-range autonomy
Undermining safeguards
Alignment faking
questions.explanation: Sandbagging is strategic underperformance during evaluation; alignment faking concerns behavior that changes when a model believes it is observed. The latter is related but names a different pattern.

questions.question: Why does the lesson recommend independent or adversarial measurement alongside lab policy thresholds?
options: Policy documents cannot mention deceptive behavior
External evaluations automatically enforce each lab's policy
Adversarial testing removes every deployment failure mode
Sandbagging can make self-reported capability measurements too low
questions.explanation: Sandbagging can make internally measured capability too low, so independent tests help check whether the estimate is reliable. Adversarial testing improves measurement but cannot remove every deployment failure.

questions.question: A policy claim says a capability is safe to deploy but gives no evaluation evidence, update cadence, or external-review status. Which reading steps should be checked?
options: Count the capabilities and categories named in the policy text.
Check evaluation evidence, declared update cadence, and review independence.
Inspect model naming and announcement language for stronger claims.
Compare the policy’s version date and length against the prior release.
questions.explanation: Check the evidence behind a claim, the declared update cadence, and review independence. Counting categories or comparing document length cannot show whether a policy is evaluated or externally scrutinized.
